source.title: D-symmetric operators: comments and some open problems

accepted.question_text: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let L(H) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on H, and call an operator A in L(H) D-symmetric when the norm closure of the range of the inner derivation δ_A(X)=AX-XA is equal to the norm closure of the range of δ_{A*}. If A and B are D-symmetric operators on H, under what conditions is their direct sum A⊕B also a D-symmetric operator?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.1. An operator A ∈ L(H) is called D-symmetric, if R(δA) = R(δA∗ ).
Question. Under what conditions the direct sum of two D-symmetric operators is a D-symmetric operator?

accepted.question_text: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let L(H) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on H. If an operator T in L(H) is called D-symmetric when the norm closure of the range of δ_T(X)=TX-XT equals the norm closure of the range of δ_{T*}, and if K denotes a compact operator on H, is the set {T+K : T is D-symmetric and K is compact} norm-closed in L(H)?
accepted.context_brief: Norm-closedness of compact perturbations of D-symmetric operators

evidence.quote: Definition 2.1. An operator A ∈ L(H) is called D-symmetric, if R(δA) = R(δA∗ ).
Now we will recall the following question posed by Joel Anderson et.al [2]. Is the set {T + K : T, D-symmetric, K compact } norm-closed in L(H)?

accepted.question_text: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For a bounded operator T on H, let δ_T be the inner derivation on L(H) defined by δ_T(X)=TX-XT. For which operators T on H does the identity operator I belong to the norm-closure of the range R(δ_T)?
accepted.context_brief: When the identity lies in a derivation range

evidence.quote: If A = B, then δA,A(X) = δA(X) = AX − XA is called the inner derivation implemented by A ∈ L(H).
Question. For which operators T on Hilbert space H do we have I ∈ R(δT )?
